title: While You Sleep, It Grows
subtitle: The seventh day belongs to the farmer who slept
teaser: Mark keeps a second seed parable: the farmer scatters, then sleeps and wakes, and the earth bears all by itself. After a week of holding the field, one day for letting it hold you.
theme: Sabbath — the growing was never ours to run; rest beside a field God keeps
framework: Mark 4:27 - the seed sprouts and grows, though he knows not how

modules.passage: Jesus also said, "The kingdom of God is like a man who scatters seed on the ground. Night and day he sleeps and wakes, and the seed sprouts and grows, though he knows not how. All by itself the earth produces a crop—first the stalk, then the head, then grain that ripens within. And as soon as the grain is ripe, he swings the sickle, because the harvest has come."
modules.transliteration: automatē hē gē karpophorei — "of itself, the earth brings forth fruit"
emphasis: Night and day he sleeps and wakes
All by itself the earth produces a crop
modules.scriptureContext: The sibling discourse's seed parable — same field, same sickle at the end, and a farmer whose main assignment between them is sleep.

modules.heading: The Farmer's Other Skill
modules.content:
Mark remembers a seed parable Matthew's discourse leaves out. A man scatters seed, and then — this is the whole middle of the story — he sleeps and wakes, night and day, while the seed sprouts and grows. He does not know how. He is not asked to know how. All by itself the earth produces, Jesus says: automatē, the old word behind our "automatic." First the stalk, then the head, then the full grain — a sequence no farmer has ever hurried.

The Preacher of Ecclesiastes gave this rest its oldest wording: no one knows the path of the wind, or how bones form in the womb, or the work of God who makes everything — so sow your seed in the morning, and let the not-knowing be. Sow, then sleep. The growing runs on power that was never in the farmer's hands, and it runs all night.

This is the seventh day, built the way God builds weeks: six days of work, then one that tells the truth about who was working the whole time. All week the field asked things of you — stillness, patience, seed. Today it asks nothing. The rows do not need watching. The growing does not need help. Rest, today, is the faith itself.

modules.inlineImageAlt: A farmer asleep under a tree at night while young shoots sprout from the dark rows on their own
modules.inlineImageCaption: Night and day he sleeps and wakes — and the earth bears, all by itself.

modules.prompt: As you rest, the one you have prayed toward all week — still far from God tonight — stands in ground that keeps working while farmers sleep. Can sleep itself say what your words have been trying to say: that the growing is God's?

modules.heading: Sabbath

scripture_anchor.text: Night and day he sleeps and wakes, and the seed sprouts and grows, though he knows not how.

modules.invitation: Do one unhurried, unproductive thing today — a walk with no phone, a slow meal, an early night. The field will not notice your absence. That is the lesson, and the gift.
modules.prayerText: Lord of the harvest, the week is Yours, the field is Yours, the growing is Yours. Teach me the farmer's other skill. I am going to sleep. Amen.
